title: How can we write two equivalent fractions for two sixths?
description: Two sixths is divided on the top and the bottom by two to get one fraction, and one third is multiplied on the top and the bottom by three to get another. A third is multiplied by four to show more are possible, and a check takes a third of each bottom number.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiplying or dividing the top and the bottom by the same number keeps the fraction equal. Watch for students who change only one of the two numbers.

source: Figure it Out Q2 (section 7.6, first block)
video_script.why: A learner writes two fractions equivalent to two sixths by dividing and multiplying the top and the bottom by the same number.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own fraction two sixths
video_script.anchor: a paper strip cut into six equal parts with two parts shaded
video_script.payoff_line: Two equivalent fractions for two sixths are one third and three ninths

final_answer.spoken: one third and three ninths, and others such as four twelfths

video_script.fraction_reading: two sixths, one third, three ninths, four twelfths
maths_rules: multiply 1/3 by 3 on top and bottom: (1 × 3)/(3 × 3) = 3/9
multiply 2/6 by 2 on top and bottom: (2 × 2)/(6 × 2) = 4/12
check: in each of 2/6, 1/3, 3/9, 4/12 the top number is one third of the bottom number
video_script.design: One idea: do the same thing to the top and the bottom. The strip with two sixths shaded stays on the board while the numbers change beside it.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a paper strip cut into 6 equal parts with 2 parts shaded, and two empty boxes beside it

marks.scene: the title card and the strip appear
marks.two: two empty boxes appear beside the strip

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about two sixths of a strip.
<bookmark mark='two'/>We want two fractions that are equivalent to two sixths.

beats.on_screen: the strip and the two empty boxes stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the strip with 2 of 6 parts shaded; pairs of sixth pieces are joined into thirds, and each part is also cut into smaller slices

marks.join: the six parts join in pairs into three bigger parts, and the two shaded parts become one
marks.cut: every part is cut into the same number of smaller slices

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Joining the parts in pairs makes fewer, bigger parts. The shaded length stays the same.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>Cutting every part into the same number of slices makes more, smaller parts.

beats.on_screen: To find: two fractions equivalent to 2/6

marks.find: the question to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find two fractions equivalent to two sixths.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: divide the numerator and the denominator by 2: (2 ÷ 2)/(6 ÷ 2) = 1/3

marks.top: an arrow marked ÷ 2 joins the 2 to a 1
marks.bottom: an arrow marked ÷ 2 joins the 6 to a 3

narration: <bookmark mark='top'/>Step one, divide the top and the bottom by two, because two divides both numbers.
<bookmark mark='bottom'/>Two divided by two is one, and six divided by two is three. We get one third.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: multiply 1/3 by 3 on top and bottom: (1 × 3)/(3 × 3) = 3/9

marks.times: an arrow marked × 3 joins the 1 to a 3 and the 3 to a 9

narration: <bookmark mark='times'/>Step two, multiply the top and the bottom of one third by three, as in your book. We get three ninths.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: others are possible: multiply 2/6 by 2 on top and bottom: (2 × 2)/(6 × 2) = 4/12
narration: <bookmark mark='more'/>Step three, other fractions work too. Multiply two sixths by two on top and bottom to get four twelfths.

beats.on_screen: Check: one third of each bottom number gives its top number: 6 gives 2, 3 gives 1, 9 gives 3, 12 gives 4

marks.check: one third of each bottom number is taken and matches the top number

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, take one third of each bottom number. It must give the top number.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 1/3 and 3/9 (others are possible, for example 4/12)

marks.pay: the answer is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Two equivalent fractions for two sixths are one third and three ninths.
Others are possible too, for example four twelfths.
